data: Android Dreams: Technological Imaginaries in Literature and Film

We often hear that technology will solve our biggest problems—inequality, governance, even loneliness. But why has technology become the main way we imagine the future at all? And what kinds of futures does it make possible—or impossible? This course approaches these questions through literature and film. We will read short stories, speculative fiction, and literary texts alongside cinema, treating them not as entertainment or illustration, but as forms of thinking—ways in which societies imagine, desire, or resist technological change. Focusing on South Asia, we will explore technological imaginaries: how narratives give shape to ideas of progress, control, care, and the human. We will practice close reading and interpretation, paying attention to voice, form, metaphor, and narrative structure, and ask how stories make technological futures imaginable.
